doc.title: Orrin Evans interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Leader versus sideman: taxes, promoters and gigs
summary: Leading means writing the music, paying people, dealing with promoters and doors, versus sidemen who learn the music and show up.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: No. Because I think you can have an idea of what you want the music to sound like as a sideman you know. I mean I think a big part of it for me being a leader, I was always a creator. I wanted to create my own gigs, I wanted to — maybe it’s the Aries in me where I needed to be in control. Whatever it is, I enjoyed that part. But it comes — it’s not easy you know. I said around tax time this year, I said, you know because everybody says why don’t you talk about the difference between the leader and the sideman. Look. You wait to tax time when you have to explain who you paid, how you paid them, you have to track all of that. There’s not just oh I showed up and I had my tunes and I got to play them. I mean it’s a whole different ballgame you know. You people when you’re — a friend of mine said the other day, “I’m a bass player. You just call me and I show up.” And I understood what he meant. As a sideman, he felt that for himself. I’m not saying I agree with that all the time. But sometimes as a sideman you learn the music and you show up. And I’m not saying that’s easy, but that’s what you do. As a leader sometimes you’ve got to write the music, show up, deal with the promoter, deal with the audience, you’re trying to play the gig and you’re watching the door to make sure you’ve got enough people to cover the — like all of that kind of stuff. And then you can deal with the music, which is not always — now I’m learning to manage and flip it you know what I mean? But it’s not easy. It’s not easy.
And then at the end of the gig you’re like hanging out to get paid and your side people are waiting to get paid. Yeah. There’s a lot to it.

Or now, like the world is, some people will say such-and-such doesn’t call me anymore. They must not like playing with me or something like that. A sideman could possibly say that. And it’s funny because some of the reasons certain people aren’t called by the leader have nothing to do with music. Sometimes I’m like okay this gig is here and they don’t drive. You know what I mean? Or this gig is here and in order to use them I’m going to have to do this, oh I can’t fly them from there. You know? So you think about all these other things that, I mean don’t really have anything to do with the music, before you get to the music. You know. Like sometimes before I decide what I’m going to play on certain gigs, I have to wait until I get the band members together. It’s not that I’m not going to play, but certain tunes I would prefer to play with certain people. It’s a whole different ballgame. And some of it has nothing to do with the desire to — your musical

thing. If you really want to do this, you know, I look at it and I see out of 365 days in the year what are Orrin Evans gigs and what are sideman gigs. And I was like obviously if I’m a leader I’ve got to get more and more gigs as Orrin Evans.
